title: Sunflower Keys — Give a listener three questions about place and pitch
summary: Try three questions about place and pitch
lead: These are things to try in the garden, not tests to pass. Each answer waits behind its own door. Keep your drawing first if you want to return to it.

questions.title: Can a moved shape keep its notes?
questions.prompt: Plant the Five-note fan, then use Copy outward. Turn on Note colors. The second group sits farther out: did it acquire five new pitches?
questions.answer: No. Seeds 0–4 and 25–29 have the same residues modulo five, so they carry the same five note colors. The places change. Copying does not by itself play either group.

questions.title: Can two places be one color?
questions.prompt: In the drawing, compare seeds 0 and 5. Then compare 0 and 1. Use the displayed seed identities rather than judging how far apart the dots look.
questions.answer: The first pair shares a color; the second does not. Note color comes from the seed number modulo five, not from the length of a line between blooms. Distance on the garden is not a pitch interval.

questions.title: Does an inversion move the middle color?
questions.prompt: Choose two different notes in a drawing, then inspect Invert colors in this section. Which one of the five colors could stay where it is? Undo after trying it.
questions.answer: Within a five-seed band, residues 0 and 4 exchange, 1 and 3 exchange, and 2 stays fixed. Only the inclusive chosen section changes. A collision or a destination outside the garden rejects the entire press, rather than trimming the phrase.

facts: Color index is seed modulo5; band reflection is 5*floor(n/5)+4−n%5. Copy offset25 preserves residues. Guide references shipped841/834 and existing Copy outward. No equal-semitone claim.
message: three authored sunflower-keys questions stay optional and leave the live experiment alone
